detailed_findings.finding: The contradiction argument is valid: from a < b and 2b <= n one gets a+b < n, so n-a-b > 0.
The algebraic identity a(n-a)-b(n-b) = (a-b)(n-a-b) is correct and is used to force the contradiction.

reason: The proof is correct and complete. Assuming a < b, it derives a+b < 2b <= n, hence n-a-b > 0, and factors the difference as a(n-a)-b(n-b) = (a-b)(n-a-b). Since a-b < 0 and n-a-b > 0, the product is negative, contradicting the hypothesis a(n-a) >= b(n-b). This matches the lemma’s intended monotonicity-on-the-first-half argument and introduces no illicit dependencies.
